items.summary: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used in software engineering, including agentic systems that coordinate multiple agents, but impose higher computational and environmental costs. In this paper, we present a comprehensive empirical study of agentic LLM systems across five software engineering tasks: code generation, technical debt identification, code vulnerability detection, log parsing, and log analysis. For each task, we compare LLM configurations that range from a non-agentic single-query baseline to multi-agent workflows, using six open-weight LLMs, two prompt strategies, and three hardware platforms. We assess each configuration in terms of accuracy, inference latency, and energy consumption. Our results reveal substantial trade-offs between agentic complexity and energy efficiency: multi-agent designs consume on average 6.36$\times$ as much energy and run 6.07$\times$ as long as the non-agentic baseline, with worst-case slowdowns of up to 160$\times$ for individual task--hardware pairs. Accuracy gains from additional agents are limited and task-specific: multi-agent improves average vulnerability-detection accuracy, but lightweight non-agentic and single-agent configurations still dominate the Pareto front, accounting for 59 of 66 Pareto-optimal configurations. Model and prompt choice act as task-specific levers whose effective direction varies between tasks rather than as global defaults. We translate these findings into design guidelines for sustainable, task-aware LLM-based development tools.
items.title: Engineering Sustainable Agents: A Systematic Comparison of Agentic LLMs for Developer Workflows

items.summary: Multi-agent systems (MAS) built from large language models coordinate specialized agents to tackle complex tasks, but effective workflows are difficult to design in advance. Test-time evolution refines workflows using execution feedback, yet broad revisions can disturb useful components, while re-executing unchanged requests can incur redundant computation. Inspired by the interplay of inheritance and selection in biological evolution, we introduce Inherit-MAS, which makes inheritance explicit at the workflow and execution levels. A meta-model first synthesizes a workflow of worker agents with declared roles, communication inputs, and tool permissions, and a separately prompted judge scores each executed candidate and diagnoses its deficiencies. In ordinary refinement rounds, \emph{workflow inheritance} starts from the latest completed candidate, may discard removable nodes judged unhelpful, and applies a validated edit to address the diagnosed deficiency. When the new candidate executes, \emph{execution inheritance} inherits eligible stored results only if the complete resolved request and execution context match, avoiding redundant model and tool calls. With GPT-4o-mini workers, Inherit-MAS achieves 55.4\% completion on WorkBench and 49.7\% joint F1 on HotpotQA FullWiki, outperforming EvoAgent, EvoMAS, and TacoMAS. With Qwen3-32B workers, it also exceeds these evolving-MAS baselines on both benchmarks. Compared with rerunning the same controller with execution inheritance disabled, execution inheritance reduces worker-token usage by 29.1\% on WorkBench and 34.6\% on HotpotQA, and total token usage by 5.3\% and 18.1\%.
items.title: Inherit-MAS: Test-Time Evolution of Multi-Agent Systems through Workflow and Execution Inheritance

items.summary: Manipulating crystal structures towards targeted geometric properties or symmetry constraints is a longstanding challenge. Existing computational frameworks fall short: LLMs have poor spatial awareness and operate at coarse granularity in the token space, while diffusion- and gradient-based structure generation approaches generally produce complete structures \textit{de novo} rather allowing for fine-grained editing of a given input under arbitrary constraints. We present LATHE, a geometric toolkit that closes this gap by expressing seven classes of crystallographic properties --- bond length, bond angle, dihedral angle, coordination environment, lattice parameters, cell volume, and space group, as differentiable objectives to enable direct geometric editing of crystal structures. To demonstrate its usage in materials design, we further expose LATHE through a Model Context Protocol server and embed it in a closed-loop multi-agent system which translates hypotheses intogeometric modifications in natural language towards a given design objective. Across single-property benchmarks, LATHE attains near-perfect constraint satisfaction on all seven property types while keeping optimized structures close to local energy minima. The LATHE-equipped agent translates over 87.5\% of natural-language prompts into valid executable configurations and faithfully completes them. In a band-gap inverse-design case study, the multi-agent loop reaches the target tolerance window in nine of ten independent runs at a typical cost of thirteen hypothesis-evaluation cycles. By bridging natural-language hypothesis generation and physically grounded gradient-based structural editing, this work establishes a paradigm for interpretable, closed-loop computational materials discovery that is immediately applicable to a broad class of functional material design tasks.
items.title: LATHE: LAnguage-driven Toolkit for Hypothesis-based crystal Editing

items.summary: Can AI agents transact? We argue that they must: as multi-agent systems (MASs) increasingly write code, deploy infrastructure, modify databases, and call web services, lost updates or stale reads can be catastrophic. Although MASs increasingly execute plans in parallel, current orchestrators do not track the state that agents read and write. As a result, concurrency anomalies manifest even in simple coding tasks. We frame MAS coordination as a data management problem and propose to describe agents by their state footprint: the state they read and write across their own local context and state, as well as the state of the orchestrator and external systems. We posit that MASs require guarantees similar to those of databases, but providing them raises new challenges and opportunities: unlike database transactions, agents do not read from a fixed schema or an isolated snapshot, and cannot be replayed deterministically upon failure. They can, however, resolve conflicts semantically instead of aborting, enabling new forms of concurrency control and conflict resolution. Towards agents that can transact, we outline a vision for next-generation agent orchestrators and transactional interfaces for external systems to participate in agentic transactions.
items.title: Tracking State Footprints: How Agents Can Transact

items.summary: Large language model (LLM)-based agents increasingly operate in multi-agent systems (MAS) characterised by strategic interaction. However, little is known about whether, and to what extent, different types of messages affect the outcomes of strategic games. By investigating AI agents based on four popular LLMs, playing four games with different cooperation equilibria, we study whether messages of different kinds (natural language, numerical signals, or random sequences) significantly modify the levels of cooperation in each game, also depending on the agents' assigned personalities. We observe that structured messages alter the final payoffs for most games and LLMs, but without a predictable pattern; this challenges the assumption that AI agents can converge to stable equilibria regardless of additional capabilities. Moreover, we observe that agent-generated numerical messages depart from randomness, most strongly and consistently when agents are explicitly instructed to communicate; however, they introduce an additional interpretability challenge, as their symbol distributions are mostly associated with the payoff structure and typically become more concentrated with repetition, but are overall difficult for humans to interpret. Monitoring for coordination of AI agents through restricted channels should thus prioritise message-level fingerprints, which generalise across models, over behavioural decisions, which do not.
items.title: When Numbers Start Talking: Numerical Signalling and Strategic Behaviour Among LLMs

items.summary: Offline multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) faces a persistent trade-off. Expressive generative policies can represent multi-modal coordination in the data, but cannot distinguish high-value regions, while value-optimized policies exploit the learned Q-function but collapse the multi-modal into a single dominant mode. A single agent's mode collapse can break joint coordination, and simultaneous drift across agents can push the joint policy into unseen regions of the action space. We propose scalable coordination via optimal unified transport (SCOUT), the first offline MARL framework to combine a generative foundation model with a learned value function through test-time action refinement. SCOUT trains two decoupled components: a flow-matching behavioral prior and a decomposed value function. At test-time, it transports behavioral samples toward high-value regions via Stein variational gradient descent. The number of transport steps controls adaptive test-time scaling, replacing a fixed regularization coefficient. Under the individual-global-max (IGM) principle, we prove a single-term KL bound on the joint soft-value gap that vanishes as transport converges, with an irreducible additive residual proportional to the IGM violation. Empirically, SCOUT achieves the best average performance across discrete and continuous offline MARL benchmarks and yields performance improvements in all offline-to-online configurations.
items.title: Test-time Multi-agent Coordination by Decomposed Value Gradient Flow

items.summary: Sunnycode v1 provides an open-access computational framework and reproducibility package supporting the research article Failure-Aware Gateway Placement and Road-Constrained Backbone Optimization for Resilient Urban LoRaWAN Networks , submitted to Digital Communications and Networks. The framework integrates OpenStreetMap (OSM) building-level sensing demand, radio-frequency (RF) feasibility, capacity-aware gateway assignment, worst-case single-gateway failure retention (N−1), gateway-load fairness, and road-constrained Steiner backbone synthesis. The repository includes Python implementations of the proposed optimization approach and four independent benchmark methods (Genetic Algorithm, Particle Swarm Optimization, Greedy, and Random Search). Dataset and experimental scope The computational experiment considers 685 building-level sensor anchors, 169 road vertices, 195 street edges, and 89 gateway candidates. The Full benchmark comprises 4,000 run-level observations obtained from 100 repetitions for each combination of five optimization methods and eight gateway budgets (k = 3–10). Repository contents Python source code and computational validation utilities. Nine original CSV files containing experimental observations, aggregated statistics, evaluation effort, and optimizer provenance. OpenStreetMap territorial input ( sunny3.osm ). Forty scientific figures in PDF format. Installation and execution instructions using Anaconda. SHA-256 file-integrity manifest and licensing information. The archived results support independent verification of the reported statistics and new computational experiments. The original historical environment metadata and detailed event histories are not included; therefore, bit-for-bit replay of the historical execution environment is not claimed. Scientific scope: RF coverage and packet delivery ratio are model-derived planning estimates rather than field-calibrated measurements. N−1 resilience represents gateway-access service retention and does not certify fault-tolerant physical-backbone connectivity. This software and dataset are released to support transparent computational research, independent assessment, and further development of resilient urban Internet of Things infrastructure planning.
items.title: Sunnycode v1 A Reproducible Framework for Failure-Aware Gateway Placement and Road-Constrained Backbone Optimization in Urban LoRaWAN Networks

items.summary: Training-free posterior sampling methods, also known as Plug-and-Play methods, leverage pretrained unconditional diffusion or flow-matching models to solve inverse problems. Most existing approaches rely on guidance weights to balance, at each time step, prior information from the unconditional score or velocity network with measurement consistency, yet the tuning of these weights is often not discussed and is largely left to heuristics. We introduce a simple and principled offline strategy for automatically tuning these guidance weights. Our key observation is that, at each time step, the conditional denoising score-matching objective for diffusion models, or the conditional flow-matching objective for flow-matching models, is a least-squares objective. Therefore, when the conditional prediction is expressed as a weighted sum of the unconditional network output and a measurement-guidance term, optimizing over these weights reduces to a two-dimensional linear least-squares problem. The resulting time-dependent guidance weights can be optimized offline for a given measurement operator, noise level and sampler at the cost of a single minibatch of sampling trajectories, without retraining or fine-tuning the pretrained generative model. Instantiated with the standard Tweedie-based measurement-consistency term, our approach improves posterior sampling and achieves state-of-the-art reconstruction performance across diffusion- and flow-matching-based methods. Moreover, the optimized guidance weights enable diffusion samplers to reduce the number of sampling steps from 1000 to 50 with no significant degradation in reconstruction quality. Code will be made available.
items.title: Getting Your Guidance Weights Right in diffusion and flow-matching posterior sampling

items.summary: Abstract   The Universal Research System with Reverse Itinerary (SUII) is a retrospective analytical methodology designed to reconstruct, in a traceable and auditable manner, the probable pathway leading from an initial problem or question to a completed scientific product. This manual brings together the universal prompt, a mandatory common core, ten core modules—including bibliographic analysis (SUII-B)—and six specialised extensions: journalistic and opinion texts (SUII-P), audiovisual or audio documents (SUII-AV), legislation and regulatory documents (SUII-L), case law and judicial decisions (SUII-J), critical appraisal of scientific articles (SUII-LC), and traceable research information management for datasets and research data objects (SUII-TRIM). Each module guides the extraction of locatable traces, classification of the epistemic status of claims, and construction of matrices linking evidence, inference, confidence, alternatives, and required verification. SUII-TRIM extends this logic to the provenance, versioning, transformation, quality control, preservation, access, and reuse of research datasets, while preserving the distinction between directly observed information, information provided by the researcher, reasoned inference, and non-determinable information. The method separates retrospective reconstruction from the prospective generation of hypotheses and requires rival explanations whenever the evidence does not support a unique conclusion. It also incorporates procedures for methodological auditing, version comparison, conceptual genealogy, peer review, algorithmic-bias assessment, external validation, teaching, and traceable research data management. SUII is not intended to recover the authors’ actual psychological history or to replace validated tools for methodological appraisal, risk-of-bias assessment, certainty of evidence, data stewardship, or repository curation. Its application requires version-controlled corpora, decision logs, retention of prompts and outputs, source verification, preservation of original data objects when applicable, and mandatory human oversight. When the available traces are insufficient, the appropriate result is “not determinable.” The manual provides practical criteria for selecting, combining, and quality-controlling the modules according to the product under analysis and the research objective, while maintaining explicit boundaries between documented evidence, reasoned inference, speculation, and unresolved uncertainty .   Resumen   El Sistema Universal de Investigación con Itinerario Inverso (SUII) es una metodología de análisis retrospectivo orientada a reconstruir, de forma trazable y auditable, el itinerario probable que conduce desde un problema o pregunta inicial hasta un producto científico finalizado. Este manual reúne el prompt universal, un núcleo común obligatorio, diez módulos nucleares y seis extensiones especializadas: análisis bibliográfico (SUII-B), textos periodísticos y de opinión (SUII-P), documentos audiovisuales o sonoros (SUII-AV), legislación y normativa (SUII-L), jurisprudencia y sentencias (SUII-J), lectura crítica de artículos científicos (SUII-LC) y gestión trazable de información y datos de investigación (SUII-TRIM). Cada módulo guía la extracción de huellas localizables, la clasificación del estado epistemológico de las afirmaciones y la construcción de matrices que relacionan evidencia, inferencia, confianza, alternativas y comprobaciones necesarias. El método separa la reconstrucción retrospectiva de la generación prospectiva de hipótesis y exige formular explicaciones rivales cuando la evidencia no permite una conclusión única. items.summary: Real-time data streams in Web of Things (WoT) and edge computing environments often evolve through latent regime changes. For online representation learning under strict computational constraints, the central problem is resolving the stability-plasticity dilemma: keeping useful historical knowledge while rapidly reacting to concept drift. Existing methods employ fixed update schedules or rolling windows. However, they suffer from parameter ossification during sudden shifts and waste computational resources when the stream remains stable. This paper proposes the Adaptive Incremental Gating System (AIGS), a lightweight closed-loop state-aware adaptation framework. AIGS introduces the Shock Ratio, an endogenous residual feedback mechanism that normalizes current reconstruction error against recent variation. This signal drives a Continuous Plasticity Controller that smoothly interpolates between learning plasticity and memory retention. By treating representation learning as a closed-loop control mechanism, AIGS avoids catastrophic forgetting and maintains a strictly linear $\mathcal{O}\left(k\cdot d\right)$ per-step complexity suitable for latency-sensitive edge devices. Experiments on real-world smart city dynamic streams-spanning traffic networks, meteorological systems, and industrial infrastructure-demonstrate distinct domain-dependent advantages. On Performance Measurement System traffic datasets, it shows significantly faster post-shift recovery after abrupt mutations. items.summary: Language functions not only as a means of transmitting information but also as a repository of cultural knowledge, collective experience, and culturally shaped patterns of thought. Consequently, translation involves more than the transfer of lexical and grammatical information between languages. It also requires the interpretation and reconstruction of meanings that are embedded within particular cultural contexts. This issue becomes especially evident in the translation of idioms, proverbs, metaphors, realia, and other culture-specific expressions whose meanings cannot always be derived from their individual lexical components. In Translation Studies, such elements are commonly discussed as culture-specific items (CSIs), which may require particular strategies to preserve their semantic, pragmatic, and cultural dimensions in the target language (Aixelá, 1996).
tags: Idiomatic expressions provide a particularly clear illustration of the relationship between language and culture.

Parameter files and output formats are unchanged. Free surface (acoustic, elastic iso/VTI/HTI/ORT, and elastic TTI solvers, 2D and 3D) Wavefield above the surface. The solvers now mirror the particle velocities above the free surface, v(−z) = v(z). Before, the top rows of the finite-difference stencils read zeros there. This made elastic surface amplitudes 6–8% too low at any mesh refinement and caused waveform errors of about 2% in acoustic media. Sources near the surface. A source whose interpolation stencil reaches the surface is injected together with its mirror image. A force is its own image. For an explosion or a moment tensor, the image removes the part that a traction-free surface cannot support. On the refined near-surface mesh, each stencil row is scaled by its own cell height. Before, the solvers dropped the stencil points on and above the surface, and force sources were not normalized by the cell height. items.summary: Abstract We present a comprehensive, universal, abstract group-theoretic, module-theoretic, and category-theoretic formalization of bijectively separated rank arithmetic . Given an arbitrary family of algebraic groups {Gi}r i=1 and elements Pi ∈ Gi with finite multiplicative orders oi = ord(Pi), we establish that the additive rank-coordinate space A(P) = Qri=1 Z/oiZ is canonically isomorphic to the external direct product of cyclic power orbits G(P) = Qri=1⟨Pi⟩ under the coordinate evaluation map ΦP(([ni]oi)i) = (Pnii)i. We prove that coordinatewise multiplication in the multiplicative state space corresponds strictly to coordinatewise addition of discrete expo- nent rank classes without introducing analytic logarithms, continuous curves, branch cuts, or topological ambiguities. We extend this framework to general category- theoretic limits, establishing that sub-space coordinate projections and factor permutation reindexings form natural transformations in the category of groups Grp. Furthermore, when lane outputs collapse into a single target background group H, we isolate the exact relation subgroup KP =ker(ΨP) and prove the quotient isomorphism A(P)/KP∼= ⟨P1, . . . , Pr⟩ ≤ H, measuring the precise algebraic information lost during scalar collapse. Finally, we formulate the extension to infinite complex power orbits , polynomial root reconstruction via Newton symmetrization of ranked power arrays Pr ∈ Cr×r, Chinese Remainder Theorem grid decompositions over composite moduli, native linear rank complexity bounds Θ(m), and an axiomatic minimal proof assistant kernel . items.summary: GradLint is a fast, standalone Rust-based command-line tool and Python package for diffusion MRI gradient-table quality control. It audits FSL and MRtrix gradient schemes, detects b-vector flip and axis-permutation errors using DWI image evidence, and writes corrected gradient tables with machine-readable provenance. GradLint is designed as a QC gate before diffusion MRI preprocessing, reconstruction, or tractography pipelines. It checks whether the supplied gradient table is geometrically consistent with the diffusion image, reports scheme-quality issues such as shell structure, direction counts, b0 handling, non-unit b-vectors, and angular sampling, and identifies silent convention errors that can otherwise propagate into tensor fitting and tractography results. The core detection method ranks signed axis permutations of the gradient table by a fibre-coherence criterion derived from a diffusion tensor fit. Candidate conventions are evaluated in the appropriate image or world frame for the input format: FSL bvec/bval tables are treated as image-relative, while MRtrix .b tables are treated as world-coordinate gradients. When a high-confidence correction is found, GradLint can emit repaired FSL and/or MRtrix gradient files together with JSON provenance describing the decision, transform, inputs, and outputs.  The software is implemented as a Rust core with thin command-line and Python interfaces. The Python package exposes the same functionality as the CLI and can render JSON reports to Markdown or HTML. Input gradient files are never modified in place unless an explicit overwrite option is used. This record archives the source code for GradLint v1.1.6, corresponding to the GitHub release published on 2026-10-03. The archived source includes the Rust core, CLI, Python bindings, report rendering layer, tests, CI/release metadata, and example materials included in the public source tree. items.summary: This protocol pre-registers a preliminary real-data study of beyond-pairwise ordinal dependence in four-variable environmental time series from Puerto Rico. It was finalized before any real-data outcome was computed. Systems. Confirmatory: (S2) daily mean discharge at four USGS gauges in the upper Río Grande de Loíza basin (50050900, 50051310, 50051800, 50055000; 1990–2025); (S4) TMAX, TMIN, AWND and WSF2 at San Juan Luis Muñoz Marín International Airport (GHCN-Daily RQW00011641; 1996–2025). Exploratory: (S1b) PM10, PM2.5 and SO2 at EPA AQS site 72-033-0004 (Cataño), combined with airport wind. Estimators. Bandt–Pompe symbols of order 3 (delay 1). The proxy excess3 = 0.6 Syn + 0.4 Surp uses fixed weights and joint-tuple counting (nested-recd 0.2.3); the pooled counting of nested-recd 0.2.2 and earlier is retained only as a reproducibility note. No-dependence references for the proxy are fitted-pairwise, independence and independent-series. Res_pair is the Kullback–Leibler divergence of the joint ordinal law from its pairwise maximum-entropy projection, obtained by iterative proportional fitting. Windows span 13 symbols; event blocks span 52 symbols. Hypotheses. H1: bias-adjusted Res_pair in blocks straddling Hurricane María (20 Sep 2017), Hurricane Fiona (18 Sep 2022) and the June 2020 Saharan dust event (Puerto Rico peak 23 Jun 2020) exceeds that of calendar-matched placebo blocks. H2: the null-referenced proxy (excess3 minus its fitted-pairwise reference) carries no information about bias-adjusted Res_pair beyond joint-symbol support (equivalence test, margin 0.30). Inference. The protocol specifies Holm multiplicity control, negative-control anchors, sensitivity analyses and decision rules. An i.i.d. parametric bootstrap from the block-fitted pairwise law is not used, because it rejected a true null in 100% of simulated 52-symbol blocks (the fitted law has far smaller support than the true law). A series-wise year-shift randomization test of cross-series independence is included as a secondary analysis; on true-null simulations at α = 0.05 its empirical size was 5.0% for chaotic and 6.7% for near-periodic independent series (pooled 5.8% over 600 tests). Negative results will be reported. Status. The pipeline has been verified on simulated coupled logistic maps only. The real-data runner remains locked until registration. Protocol revisions, including correction of a counting error in the Syn term of nested-recd identified during re-analysis of simulated data, are logged in Section 16 of the protocol; all were made before any real-data outcome was computed. Version 0.3.1 is a prose-only polish of the protocol documents, with no scientific changes.

items.summary: CORE-LLM-Bench is a controlled neurosymbolic benchmark for evaluating ontology-grounded reasoning in large language models. Version 1.1.0 contains 9,048 unique question-hop instances derived from four ontology datasets: Family, Pizza 100, Pizza 250, and OWL2Bench. The benchmark contains 6,032 binary question-answering (BQA) instances and 3,016 open-ended question-answering (OEQA) instances. Benchmark instances support 1-hop and 2-hop ontology contexts and aligned natural-language (NL), formal-symbolic (FS), and entity-abstracted (AR) representations. Ground-truth answers and explanation structures are derived using symbolic ontology reasoning, enabling controlled evaluation according to task formulation, representation, semantic abstraction, context depth, explanation-based reasoning complexity, and reasoning type. The release includes benchmark data, reasoning metadata, provenance and licensing documentation, release manifests and checksums, and scripts supporting benchmark generation, validation, Hugging Face export, and reproducibility. items.summary: Can AI agents transact? We argue that they must: as multi-agent systems (MASs) increasingly write code, deploy infrastructure, modify databases, and call web services, lost updates or stale reads can be catastrophic. Although MASs increasingly execute plans in parallel, current orchestrators do not track the state that agents read and write. As a result, concurrency anomalies manifest even in simple coding tasks. We frame MAS coordination as a data management problem and propose to describe agents by their state footprint: the state they read and write across their own local context and state, as well as the state of the orchestrator and external systems. We posit that MASs require guarantees similar to those of databases, but providing them raises new challenges and opportunities: unlike database transactions, agents do not read from a fixed schema or an isolated snapshot, and cannot be replayed deterministically upon failure. They can, however, resolve conflicts semantically instead of aborting, enabling new forms of concurrency control and conflict resolution. Towards agents that can transact, we outline a vision for next-generation agent orchestrators and transactional interfaces for external systems to participate in agentic transactions.
items.title: Tracking State Footprints: How Agents Can Transact

items.summary: Multi-agent systems (MAS) built from large language models coordinate specialized agents to tackle complex tasks, but effective workflows are difficult to design in advance. Test-time evolution refines workflows using execution feedback, yet broad revisions can disturb useful components, while re-executing unchanged requests can incur redundant computation. Inspired by the interplay of inheritance and selection in biological evolution, we introduce Inherit-MAS, which makes inheritance explicit at the workflow and execution levels. A meta-model first synthesizes a workflow of worker agents with declared roles, communication inputs, and tool permissions, and a separately prompted judge scores each executed candidate and diagnoses its deficiencies. In ordinary refinement rounds, \emph{workflow inheritance} starts from the latest completed candidate, may discard removable nodes judged unhelpful, and applies a validated edit to address the diagnosed deficiency. When the new candidate executes, \emph{execution inheritance} inherits eligible stored results only if the complete resolved request and execution context match, avoiding redundant model and tool calls. With GPT-4o-mini workers, Inherit-MAS achieves 55.4\% completion on WorkBench and 49.7\% joint F1 on HotpotQA FullWiki, outperforming EvoAgent, EvoMAS, and TacoMAS. With Qwen3-32B workers, it also exceeds these evolving-MAS baselines on both benchmarks. Compared with rerunning the same controller with execution inheritance disabled, execution inheritance reduces worker-token usage by 29.1\% on WorkBench and 34.6\% on HotpotQA, and total token usage by 5.3\% and 18.1\%.

items.summary: This deposit contains the empirical backbone of the companion article Structural reconfiguration of cultural industries under AI micro-dramas: measurement, mechanisms and scenarios : the cleaned datasets, the complete Python replication pipeline, and the provenance documentation that traces every number in the paper back to a public, checkable source. Contents 74 datasets (19 raw, 55 analysis-ready) covering four studies: (1) a content-level panel of 2,938 coded entries from platform drama rankings, with 2,299 items in the analysis panel; (2) a sector wage and output panel for the creative industries with an AI-exposure classification; (3) a cross-country box-office panel used for synthetic-control identification checks; and (4) a 2030 scenario analysis with 10,000 Monte Carlo draws (fixed seed 20260929). 27 replication scripts (Python 3.13) forming the full pipeline from data collection through analysis to figure generation. An English data codebook listing every dataset and field name, and a data provenance audit recording the source, verification tier and caveats of every series. A file inventory with SHA-256 checksums. Provenance and verification Every row of every raw dataset carries source , verify and note fields. Three verification tiers are used: verified (official body or authoritative report), pending (second-hand or conflicting), and caliber disputed (institutions report materially different values for the same indicator). Of the 181 rows carrying a tier, 150 are verified, 21 pending and 10 disputed. Where institutions disagree — most visibly on the size of the micro-drama market and on cross-country box office — all calibers are retained rather than silently resolved, because the disagreement is itself evidence. Three handling rules apply throughout: zero imputation (missing stays missing), provenance on every row, and calibers bound to their numbers (no cross-caliber subtraction or ratios). Not included Third-party webpage content collected during coding (cached article HTML) is not redistributed; only the author's own coded fields and the source URLs are released. The bibliographic library used for the literature review is third-party metadata retrievable from Crossref and OpenAlex, and is available on request. See REPRODUCE.md for the full command sequence and runtime notes. Directory names are kept in the original project layout so that the scripts run unmodified.

items.summary: Table-to-report generation refers to the task of automatically generating article-level analyt- ical reports from relational tables and is an essential capability for automated data science and decision support. Its central challenge lies in systematically discovering verifiable com- posite insights across tables, attributes, and analytical perspectives, and organizing them into coherent, complete, and traceable evidence chains. Existing methods primarily rely on sequential, reactive data agents or direct Large Language Model(LLM) generation. They suffer from exploration bias: early local observations constrain subsequent actions, causing models to focus prematurely on local analyzes and miss cross-table or cross-dimensional evidence. We propose ComInsight, which reformulates insight discovery as the composition of atomic evidences. We first define an atomic insight as the smallest executable analytical unit conforming to a predefined analysis pattern and enumerate all valid atomic insights from database schema and content. These atoms are then organized into a multi-relational insight graph, where nodes represent verified data facts and edges encode logical, temporal, or hierarchical relations. Finally, a set of composition operators systematically fuses atomic nodes into higher-order composite conclusions. Every composite output is accompanied by executable SQL and fine-grained provenance, ensuring full verifiability. Across three benchmarks InsightBench, DDR-Bench, and T2R-Bench, ComInsight consistently outperforms strong baselines in factual correctness, novelty, and structural completeness. We believe ComInsight offers a reliable, efficient, and explainable path toward table-to-report generation.
items.title: Structured Composition of Verifiable Atomic Insights for Table-to-Report Generation
